subject: Re: Northwind AI usage discrepancy : suspected retries/stream cancellation
thread_body:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 9:27 AM
Subject: Northwind AI usage discrepancy: suspected retries/stream cancellation

Looping you in on a customer escalation. Northwind is seeing ~18-25% higher usage (token totals) than their internal estimates.

Hypotheses:
- client timeouts + retry  we count each attempt
- streaming cancellation: do we count tokens emitted before cancel? do we count prompt tokens even if generation cancelled?
- dashboard aggregation maybe double-counting on certain response codes

Attachment: northwind-request-samples.csv (request ids + timestamps they provided)

Can someone from platform/usage pipeline sanity check the accounting for retries + stream disconnects?


From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind AI usage discrepancy: suspected retries/stream cancellation

Thanks. Two things:
1) usage pipeline counts per-attempt, not per logical request. If client retries, that will look inflated vs their expected.
2) prompt tokens are counted once the request is admitted; cancellation doesnt undo prompt tokens. completion tokens should be only what we actually stream.

We should confirm if their library retries on 499/timeout.


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 10:18 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind AI usage discrepancy: suspected retries/stream cancellation

+1. Also: the UI currently groups by request_id (which is attempt id). Some customers think its an id they generate and stable across retries.

If we can add UI text: Each retry is billed as a separate attempt that might solve a bunch of these.


From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 11:06 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind AI usage discrepancy: suspected retries/stream cancellation

Customer uses a homegrown gateway and they do retry once on timeout. They assumed the timeout attempt doesnt count if they didnt get the full answer.

They also have client-side 15s timeout; they cancel streams.


From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 12:22 PM
Subject: Re: Northwind AI usage discrepancy: suspected retries/stream cancellation

Ok. This sounds expected behavior, but our comms are weak. Ill drop a note in #support + #eng-platform and we should capture in known-issues/workarounds.

We should still ensure were not double counting completion tokens on partial streams. Ill verify with logs today.


From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Thanks. If its expected, we may still want a one-time credit for goodwill (CS can decide), but would prefer to avoid setting precedent. Lets first get a crisp explanation + recommended client config (timeout, retry, idempotency).
